st_lavoir.name: Passage des Nœuds
st_lavoir.alt: A sunny wooden deck on stilts along the blue canal by the old wash-house, with a rowing boat moored to a post, an iron bollard, a bench and a canary in its cage on a barrel; four painted doors stand along the back: yellow in the wash-house, red in the boat shed, blue in the stone cottage across the footbridge and green in the ivy-covered wall. Monsieur Verbe polishes a black boot with wax on his crate; scratches his head, puzzled; unclips the beagle's lead from the bollard; ties the boat's rope in a big knot round the post; hammers a nail into the bench; and drapes a cloth over the canary's cage. The cobbled lane on the left leads back to the houses.

doors.label: Rue des Torchons
doors.hint: Through the green door in the ivy wall

balayeurs.name: Rue des Balayeurs
balayeurs.alt: Inside the open-sided old wash-house over the canal, with a round stone washing basin full of suds, white sheets hanging from the beams, a clean sheet spread on the flagstones and a shiny brass basin: Monsieur Verbe stares at the mud splashed all over his stripes in a green beret; gasps as a muddy puppy leaves paw prints on the clean sheet; lifts a snow-white shirt out of the suds in a green beret; shields his eyes from a dazzling flash of light in a green beret; sweeps the petals with a big broom; and holds a carnival mask over his face. The yellow door leads back.

repasser.name: Allée du Fer-à-Repasser
repasser.alt: A grassy drying green on the canal bank beside the wooden boat shed, with a washing line between two posts and a gate chained shut on a flock of geese: Monsieur Verbe irons a shirt on the ironing board; pulls the chain off the gate as the geese burst out honking; shivers and rubs his hands together; dunks a croissant into a big bowl; pegs a shirt on the washing line; and kneels by an open treasure chest beside Grandma's portrait, lifting out her necklace. The red door of the boat shed leads back.

doors.label: Passage des Nœuds
doors.hint: Back through the red boat-shed door

clowns.name: Ruelle des Clowns
clowns.alt: A canal towpath where a circus barge with bunting is moored, with a striped circus tent on the bank, a big tree with a spider dangling from a branch, a little hurdle and a paper hoop on a stand: Monsieur Verbe paints on a round red clown nose in his hand mirror; swirls a long blue cloak over his shoulders in a gold beret; goes pale green with fright as the spider drops in front of his nose, in a green beret; leaps over the hurdle in a green beret; bursts through the paper hoop; and digs a hole with his spade. The blue door across the footbridge leads back.

doors.label: Passage des Nœuds
doors.hint: Back over the footbridge, through the blue door

torchons.name: Rue des Torchons
torchons.alt: The lock-keeper's cottage garden beside the canal, with checked tea towels on a line, a garden chair, a crooked picture on an easel, a birdhouse on a pole, a table with a tipped-over milk jug and a box of lettuces under a little grey hail cloud: Monsieur Verbe massages the shoulders of a smiling old gentleman; wipes a wet plate with a checked tea towel; straightens the picture on the easel; holds up the birdhouse as a bluebird flies in; blushes pink over the spilt milk; and clutches his head as the hail flattens his lettuces, in a green beret. The green garden door leads back.

doors.label: Passage des Nœuds
doors.hint: Back through the green garden door
